v.rationale: Both implementations pass their own suites (52 and 45 tests), are structurally similar, and share the old() checkbox bug: a browser leaves an unticked box out of the submitted form, so after a failed submit the Active box comes back ticked. Probes confirmed this in both. impl-1 ranks first. It has a cleaner domain model: a ProductSort enum validated with Rule::enum, a typed sort() accessor, dollar-to-cent conversion inside the FormRequest, and category_id kept out of fillable by using the relationship. It also eager-loads category for related products. Its filter form reuses the field components, so errors appear next to each filter, and it uses @session and __() consistently. Its main extra flaw is the backslash escape clause in the LIKE search, which breaks on MySQL. impl-2 has a real N+1 on the product page (4 lazy category loads, confirmed by probe). It puts more logic and styling in views (@php in the form, inline styles, the view reaching into a FormRequest constant), writes the filter form by hand without per-field errors, and makes admins enter prices in cents. Its tests are solid but contain a hard-coded id and leftover Pest.php boilerplate.
